cluster_summary: This cluster contains vulnerabilities where untrusted input (serialized data, JSON, configuration) specifies a class name that is then loaded or instantiated without sufficient validation—either an allowlist or a comprehensive blocklist. Most members involve incomplete deny-lists in polymorphic deserialization frameworks, allowing instantiation of dangerous gadget classes. A few members involve missing allowlists in reflective instantiation or resource exhaustion from recursive collection structures.
guideline_text: Trace untrusted serialized bytes, object streams, pickles, marshaled payloads, or type metadata into deserializers that instantiate classes, reconstruct object graphs, or invoke callbacks during object creation. Report code paths where allowed classes, object types, and construction side effects are not constrained before deserialization. Confirm that the guard is enforced before the sensitive effect and remains bound to the same resource, principal, destination, or object that the effect uses. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 9 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should use type allowlists, safe codecs, signature checks, or data-only formats instead of general object deserialization.

mechanism.missing_guard: allowed classes, object types, and construction side effects are not constrained before deserialization
mechanism.name: untrusted deserialization with attacker-controlled type graph
mechanism.sink_shape: deserializers that instantiate classes, reconstruct object graphs, or invoke callbacks during object creation
mechanism.source_shape: untrusted serialized bytes, object streams, pickles, marshaled payloads, or type metadata
mechanism.typical_fix: use type allowlists, safe codecs, signature checks, or data-only formats instead of general object deserialization

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add the missing dangerous class names to the static blocklist (e.g., DEFAULT_NO_DESER_CLASS_NAMES) and maintain an up-to-date comprehensive blocklist.
sub_patterns.name: Incomplete blocklist in polymorphic deserialization frameworks
sub_patterns.root_cause: Deserialization frameworks rely on a static deny-list of dangerous classes to prevent instantiation of gadget chains, but the list is incomplete, allowing attackers to specify unlisted dangerous classes that can trigger arbitrary code execution, JNDI injection, or XXE.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Explicitly reject any type that is a subclass of Throwable when autoType is disabled, and extend the deny hash list for known dangerous classes.
sub_patterns.name: AutoType bypass via unhandled Throwable subclasses
sub_patterns.root_cause: When autoType is disabled, the code only rejects Exception types but not Error or other Throwable subclasses, allowing attackers to deserialize dangerous classes ending with 'Error' or other suffixes.
